en: to be frivolous; to be silly

examples.ko: 그는 실없는 농담으로 분위기를 풀어 줬어요.
examples.en: He eased the mood with a silly joke.

examples.ko: 말이 너무 실없어서 아무도 진지하게 안 들었어요.
examples.en: His talk was so frivolous that nobody took it seriously.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 가끔 실없어 보여도 속은 깊어요.
examples.en: That person sometimes seems flippant, but he is deep inside.

examples.ko: 실없을 때가 많지만 정이 많은 친구예요.
examples.en: He is often silly, but he's a warm-hearted friend.
Why are you being so silly today?

examples.ko: 실없다고 놀림을 받아도 그는 개의치 않았어요.
examples.en: Even when teased for being flippant, he didn't mind.

explain: 농담이나 말, 웃음이 가볍고 진지하지 않을 때 쓰고, 보통 '실없는 소리/농담/웃음'처럼 붙여서 말해요. 칭찬은 아니라서 상대에게 직접 말하면 기분이 나쁠 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 실없는 소리 그만하고 일 좀 해요.
phrases.en: Stop the silly talk and get some work done.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍고 쓸데없는 말을 가리키는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for light and pointless talk.

phrases.example: 그는 대답 대신 실없는 웃음만 지었어요.
phrases.en: Instead of answering, he just gave a frivolous smile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진지하지 않고 가벼운 웃음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a light, unserious smile.

phrases.example: 그렇게 자꾸 웃으면 좀 실없어 보여요.
phrases.en: If you keep laughing like that, you look a bit frivolous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 가벼워 보인다는 뜻으로, 상대에게 직접 말하면 무례할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone looks flighty, which can be rude to say to their face.

explain_en: It describes jokes, words or laughter that are light and not serious, and usually appears as '실없는 소리/농담/웃음'. It is not a compliment, so saying it directly to someone may upset them.

examples.ko: 아이들이 말을 안 들어서 속을 썩여요.
examples.en: The kids don't listen, so they cause me a lot of worry.

examples.ko: 제발 엄마 속 좀 그만 썩이세요.
examples.en: Please stop worrying your mom so much.

examples.ko: 부모님 속을 썩인 일이 지금도 마음에 걸려요.
examples.en: I still feel bad about the times I troubled my parents.

examples.ko: 학생 때 선생님 속을 많이 썩였어요.
examples.en: When I was a student, I gave my teachers a lot of trouble.

examples.ko: 자꾸 속을 썩이면 친구들도 떠나갈 거예요.
examples.en: If you keep causing trouble, even your friends will leave.

examples.ko: 우리 강아지는 아직도 말썽을 피워서 속을 썩이는 중이에요.
examples.en: Our puppy is still causing mischief and giving me a hard time.

explain: 거의 '속을 썩이다' 모양으로 쓰고, 말썽이나 걱정거리 때문에 다른 사람을 힘들게 한다는 느낌이에요. 힘든 사람이 주어이면 '속이 썩다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 동생이 자꾸 말썽을 부려서 부모님 속을 썩여요.
phrases.en: cause someone grief
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 썩는다는 뜻과 관계없이, 누군가를 마음고생하게 만든다는 관용 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An idiom meaning to cause someone mental distress, unrelated to food rotting.

phrases.en: be worried sick
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정과 마음고생이 너무 커서 속이 상한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Worry and distress are so great that one is sick at heart.

explain_en: It almost always appears as '속을 썩이다' and means causing someone worry or trouble through bad behavior. When the suffering person is the subject, say '속이 썩다' instead.

t90.ax: Please stop worrying your mom so much.

en: to be idiotic; to be dumb; to be foolish

examples.ko: 그 사람은 좀 어벙해 보여도 일은 잘해요.
examples.en: He may look a bit dopey, but he does his job well.

examples.ko: 어벙한 표정으로 서 있지 말고 도와줘요.
examples.en: Don't just stand there looking blank; help me.

examples.ko: 내 동생은 어벙해서 자주 물건을 잃어버려요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is a bit spacey and often loses things.
I acted spacey and made a mistake.
The friend who seemed goofy at first is now a team leader.
Why are you so out of it today?

explain: 조금 모자라거나 멍해 보이는 사람이나 행동을 편하게 말할 때 써요. 놀리는 느낌이 있어서 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.

phrases.en: That child looked a bit dopey at first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 모자라거나 멍해 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone looks a little slow or dazed on the surface.

phrases.en: He looked at me with a blank, dopey expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어벙하다'를 명사 앞에 붙인 꼴로, 멍한 얼굴을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun, describing a blank face.

phrases.en: My brother isn't dopey. He is thoughtful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉보기와 달리 모자라지 않다고 부정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to deny that someone is foolish, despite appearances.

explain_en: It is a casual word for someone or something that seems a bit dim or spaced out. It has a teasing tone, so avoid using it about people older than you or people you've just met.

examples.en: The child acts spoiled with its mother.
The youngest acts very spoiled in front of Dad.

examples.ko: 그만 응석 부리고 혼자 해 보세요.
examples.en: Stop acting spoiled and try doing it on your own.
My younger sibling is both clingy and teary.

examples.ko: 응석만 부리지 말고 스스로 해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't just act spoiled, try doing it by yourself.

examples.ko: 아이의 응석은 다 받아 주면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't give in to all of a child's whining.

explain: 보통 '응석을 부리다', '응석을 받아 주다'처럼 짝으로 써요. '어리광'과 비슷하지만, 어른이 응석을 부리면 철이 없다는 느낌이 들 수 있어요. 가까운 사람에게 기대고 싶어서 하는 행동이에요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling acts spoiled with Mom.
phrases.nuance_ko: '응석'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb most often paired with '응석'.

phrases.example: 할머니는 손주의 응석을 다 받아 주세요.
phrases.en: Grandma gives in to all of her grandchild's whims.
phrases.nuance_ko: 응석을 부리는 사람을 너그럽게 대해 준다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means tolerating and indulging someone who acts spoiled.

phrases.example: 동생이 태어난 뒤로 첫째의 응석이 늘었어요.
phrases.en: Since the baby was born, the eldest's clinginess has grown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 응석 부리는 일이 점점 많아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when acting spoiled becomes more frequent.

explain_en: It is usually used in pairs like '응석을 부리다' (act spoiled) and '응석을 받아 주다' (indulge someone). It is close to '어리광', but when an adult does it, it can sound immature. It is behavior from wanting to lean on someone close.

en: to depend on; to rely on; to be dependent

examples.en: The child depends too much on his parents.

examples.ko: 저는 지도 앱에 의존해서 길을 찾아요.
examples.en: I rely on a map app to find my way.
This shop depends on tourists.
I want to live without relying on others.
I want to fix my habit of depending on my smartphone.

examples.ko: 우리나라는 에너지를 수입에 의존할 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: Our country has no choice but to rely on imports for energy.

explain: 사람에게는 '에게', 사물이나 나라에는 '에'를 붙여 '~에게/에 의존하다'로 써요. '의지하다'는 마음으로 기대는 따뜻한 느낌이고, '의존하다'는 지나치게 기댄다는 느낌이 들 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 친구에게 너무 의존해서 혼자 못 해요.
phrases.en: I rely on my friend too much, so I can't do it alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유나 방법을 이어서 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form for giving a reason or a means.

phrases.en: I don't depend on my parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 해결한다는 뜻을 나타내는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, showing that you handle things yourself.

phrases.en: When it's hard, I lean on my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의존하다'보다 마음으로 기대는 따뜻한 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Warmer than 의존하다, with the feeling of leaning on someone emotionally.

explain_en: Relying on a person or thing for needs; can imply dependence. Attach 에게 for people and 에 for things or countries: '~에게/에 의존하다'. 의지하다 has a warm feeling of leaning on someone emotionally, while 의존하다 can suggest leaning too much.

en: to raise up; to hold up straight; to praise highly

examples.ko: 그는 부탁을 하려고 나를 한참 추켜세웠어요.
examples.en: He flattered me for quite a while to ask a favor.
If you praise me too much, it actually feels like pressure.
If you build a child up with praise, they gain confidence.
It was cold, so I walked with my collar turned up.
The teacher raised their eyebrows as if surprised.

examples.ko: 사장님은 일부러 직원들을 추켜세우며 일을 시켰어요.
examples.en: The boss deliberately flattered the employees while giving them work.

explain: 옷깃이나 눈썹을 위로 올리는 뜻 외에, 사람을 지나치게 칭찬해 띄워 줄 때 많이 써요. '칭찬하다'는 중립적이지만 '추켜세우다'는 과하거나 겉치레, 때로는 속셈이 있는 칭찬 느낌이에요. '치켜세우다'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰여요.

phrases.en: His friends praise him so much that he feels uncomfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: '추켜세우다'와 같은 뜻이라서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 추켜세우다, so the two can be used interchangeably.

phrases.en: He raised his eyebrows in surprise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 대신 몸의 일부를 위로 올린다는 원래 뜻으로 쓴 예예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the original meaning of lifting a body part upward.

phrases.en: Please don't flatter me so much. I'm embarrassed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과한 칭찬을 부드럽게 말리고 싶을 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentle way to ask someone to stop over-the-top praise.

explain_en: Raise something upright; also to flatter or praise (막대기를 추켜세우다) Besides lifting a collar or eyebrows upward, it is often used for praising someone excessively and building them up. '칭찬하다' is neutral, but '추켜세우다' feels over-the-top, superficial, or sometimes done with a hidden motive. '치켜세우다' is used with the same meaning.

t90.ax: He flattered me for quite a while to ask a favor.

examples.en: She raised someone else's child like her own.
Whether biological or adopted, they are all precious family.
My grandmother cherishes her daughter-in-law like her own child.
He isn't my own child, but we've grown very close.
They say there are secrets that are hard to tell even your own child.
Thank you for treating me as well as your own child.

explain: 직접 낳은 자식을 말해요. 남을 아주 가깝게 대할 때 '친자식처럼'이라는 비유로도 많이 써요. 새 배우자의 자식은 '의붓자식'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My grandmother cared for me like her own child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 가깝게 대한다는 비유로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as a metaphor for treating someone very close.

phrases.en: That student is like my own child to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 가까운 사람에게 느끼는 정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses affection for someone you feel close to.

phrases.en: That child is not their biological child but an adopted one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혈연 관계를 구분해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to distinguish blood relationships.

explain_en: Everyday word for one's own birth child, often compared with adopted or other children (친자식처럼) It means a child you gave birth to yourself. It is also often used figuratively as '친자식처럼' (like one's own child) for treating others very warmly. A new spouse's child is called '의붓자식'.

t90.ax: She raised someone else's child like her own.

examples.ko: 엄마가 아이 등을 토닥토닥 두드려 줬어요.
examples.en: Mom gently patted the child's back.
Saying 'It's okay,' I gave her shoulder gentle pats.
The baby drifted off to sleep to the sound of soft patting.

examples.ko: 토닥토닥 위로해 주는 친구가 있어서 힘이 나요.
examples.en: I have a friend who comforts me with gentle pats, and it gives me strength.
I gave the puppy's head gentle pats.
Raindrops are tapping lightly against the window.

explain: 가볍고 다정하게 두드리는 모습이나 소리를 말해요. 위로하는 장면에 잘 어울려서, 메신저에서 위로하는 마음을 '토닥토닥'이라고 쓰기도 해요. 빗방울이 약하게 떨어지는 소리에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I soothed the crying baby with gentle pats.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우는 사람을 달랠 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for comforting someone who is crying.

phrases.en: My friend gave my shoulder a comforting pat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '토닥토닥'에서 나온 동사로, 위로하는 몸짓을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb from 토닥토닥 that describes a comforting gesture.

phrases.en: I sent a message saying, 'Cheer up, there there.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 메신저에서 위로하는 마음을 짧게 보낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short way to send comfort in a messenger chat.

explain_en: It describes the look or sound of light, tender patting. It suits comforting scenes, and people even type '토닥토닥' in chats to show comfort. It can also describe the sound of light raindrops.

t90.ax: Mom gently patted the child's back.

examples.ko: 신입 사원은 아직 햇병아리라서 실수가 많아요.
examples.en: The new employee is still a rookie, so he makes many mistakes.
When it comes to cooking, I'm a complete beginner.
When I was a rookie, my seniors helped me a lot.
I went to the countryside to see the newly hatched chicks at the farm.
Thank you for giving a rookie like me a chance.
He's a rookie reporter, but his questions are sharp.

explain: 원래는 막 깬 병아리인데, 사람에게 쓰면 경험이 거의 없는 초보를 가리켜요. 스스로 낮춰 말할 때는 겸손하게 들리지만, 남에게 쓰면 얕보는 느낌이 날 수 있어요. 비슷한 말은 '초보', '신참'이에요.

phrases.en: I'm still a beginner at driving.
phrases.nuance_ko: '햇병아리'보다 평범하고 부드러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plainer, softer word than 햇병아리.

phrases.en: I'm new here, so I'm still clumsy at the work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 들어온 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone who has newly joined.

phrases.en: I'm a green newbie, so there is a lot I don't know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로를 낮추어 겸손하게 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits when humbly describing yourself.

explain_en: It originally means a freshly hatched chick, but for people it points to a beginner with almost no experience. Used about yourself it sounds humble, but about someone else it can sound belittling. Similar words are '초보' and '신참'.

t90.ax: Thank you for giving a rookie like me a chance.

en: to sacrifice oneself; to give up something for others

examples.ko: 부모님은 우리를 위해 많은 것을 희생하셨어요.
examples.en: My parents sacrificed a lot for us.

examples.ko: 가족을 위해 시간을 희생해야 할 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes you have to give up your time for your family.
Don't work at the cost of your health.

examples.ko: 친구를 구하려고 자신을 희생한 사람 이야기를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read about a person who sacrificed himself to save a friend.

examples.ko: 저는 꿈을 위해 잠을 희생하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm sacrificing sleep for my dream.
A heart that sacrifices for everyone is remarkable.

explain: '~을 위해 ~을 희생하다'처럼 포기하는 것과 위하는 대상을 같이 말해요. 자기가 선택해서 내놓는다는 점이 '희생되다'와 달라요. 부모님, 가족 이야기에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I don't want to sacrifice my health.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 포기하고 싶지 않은지 '을/를'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '을/를' to say what you don't want to give up.

phrases.en: That firefighter has a strong spirit of self-sacrifice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남을 위해 자신을 내놓는 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the willingness to give up something for others.

phrases.example: 가족을 위해 희생하는 부모님께 늘 감사해요.
phrases.en: I'm always grateful to my parents, who sacrifice for the family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 앞에서 꾸며 주어 어떤 사람인지 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies a noun to describe someone who sacrifices.

explain_en: Active; you willingly give up something for others. Say what is given up and who it is for, as in '~을 위해 ~을 희생하다'. Unlike '희생되다', the person chooses to give it up. It suits talk about parents and family.

dis.h: willingly give yourself up for others
gh: be sacrificed; fall victim to something

examples.en: The night sea looked a blackish blue.
The sky turned dark blue and then the rain poured down.
The bruise was dark blue and looked painful.

examples.ko: 새벽 네 시라 하늘이 아직 검푸르렀어요.
examples.en: It was four in the morning, so the sky was still dark blue.
Deep seawater looks dark blue and cold.

examples.ko: 숲이 짙어서 산이 멀리서 보면 검푸르러요.
examples.en: The forest is thick, so the mountain looks dark blue from far away.

explain: 검은빛이 도는 짙은 푸른색을 말해요. 깊은 바다, 밤하늘, 짙은 숲, 멍처럼 어둡고 깊은 느낌에 많이 써요. '푸르다'처럼 '러' 불규칙이라서 '검푸르러요', '검푸르렀어요'가 돼요.

phrases.en: I looked at the dark blue sea from the ship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the form used to describe a noun that follows.

phrases.en: The night sky is dark blue.
phrases.nuance_ko: '러' 불규칙이라 '검푸르어요'가 아니라 '검푸르러요'가 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Because it is a 러-irregular, it becomes 검푸르러요, not 검푸르어요.

phrases.en: The clouds turned dark blue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이 바뀌는 모습을 말할 때 '-게'로 바꿔 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Change it to -게 to describe a color changing.

explain_en: It describes a deep blue with a touch of black. It is often used for deep sea, night sky, thick forest or bruises, giving a dark, deep feeling. Like '푸르다', it is a '러' irregular, so it becomes '검푸르러요' and '검푸르렀어요'.

examples.en: The willow branches sway gently in the spring breeze.
Willow branches hang long by the stream.
My grandmother made a basket out of willow branches.
Buds have started to sprout on the willow branches.

examples.ko: 연못 옆 버들가지 아래에서 잠깐 쉬었어요.
examples.en: I rested for a while under the willow branches by the pond.

examples.ko: 이 오래된 노래에는 버들가지 이야기가 나와요.
examples.en: This old song mentions willow branches.

explain: 버드나무의 가늘고 긴 가지예요. 아래로 늘어진 모습 때문에 봄 풍경을 말할 때 자주 나와요. '버들'은 버드나무를 뜻하는 말로, '버들잎'처럼 다른 말과도 붙어요.

phrases.en: New buds came out on the willow branch.
phrases.nuance_ko: '버들가지'를 풀어서 말한 표현이라 설명할 때 쓰기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out way of saying 버들가지, handy when explaining.

phrases.en: The willow leaves sway in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가지가 아니라 잎만 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you mean only the leaves, not the branches.

phrases.en: I broke off a willow branch by the stream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버들가지를 손으로 만지고 다루는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes physically handling willow branches.
phrases.en_equiv: to snap off a willow branch

explain_en: These are the thin, long branches of a willow tree. Because they hang down gracefully, they often appear when describing spring scenery. '버들' refers to the willow tree and also combines with other words, as in '버들잎'.

examples.en: This bird lives in the forest.
The fish lived in the clean river.
I researched the animals that live in the Arctic.

examples.ko: 그 식물은 습한 곳에 서식하기 때문에 물이 중요해요.
examples.en: That plant grows in damp places, so water is important.

examples.ko: 개발 때문에 동물이 서식할 곳이 줄어들었어요.
examples.en: Because of development, the places where animals can live have shrunk.
Countless living things inhabit the sea.

explain: 서식하다는 동물이나 식물이 어떤 곳에서 살아가는 거예요. 사람이 사는 것에는 쓰지 않고 '살다'나 '거주하다'를 써요. '서식지'는 동물이나 식물이 사는 곳이에요.

phrases.en: This place is a habitat for birds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이나 식물이 사는 곳을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun for the place where animals or plants live.

phrases.example: 이 강에는 여러 물고기가 서식하고 있어요.
phrases.en: Various fish live in this river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 그곳에서 살고 있다는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say they currently live there.

phrases.en: I observed the animals that live in the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서식하는'이 뒤에 오는 동물이나 식물을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: 서식하는 modifies the animal or plant that follows.

explain_en: 서식하다 is for animals or plants living in a certain place. For people, use '살다' or '거주하다' instead. 서식지 is the habitat where such animals or plants live.

examples.en: Old dialects are gradually dying out.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 오래전에 소멸되어서 지도에 없어요.
examples.en: That country disappeared long ago, so it is not on the map.

examples.ko: 쓰지 않는 단어는 시간이 지나면 소멸돼요.
examples.en: Words that are not used die out over time.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 사람이 줄어서 소멸될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: This village could vanish because its people are decreasing.

examples.ko: 소멸된 문화를 책으로 다시 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: I learned again about a vanished culture through a book.

examples.ko: 기간이 지나면 포인트가 소멸되니까 빨리 쓰세요.
examples.en: Points expire after the period, so use them quickly.

explain: '소멸되다'는 있던 것이 완전히 없어질 때 써요. 일상에서는 '사라지다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '소멸되다'는 언어, 마을, 권리처럼 큰 것이 서서히 없어질 때 어울려요. 카드의 포인트나 쿠폰이 기간이 지나서 없어질 때도 '소멸되다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The points expire after one month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기간이 지나서 포인트나 쿠폰이 없어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when points or coupons disappear after their period.

phrases.example: 이 언어는 곧 소멸될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This language could die out soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 없어질 가능성이 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something might disappear.

phrases.en: It's a village at risk of disappearing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 없어질 것 같은 상태를 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pair for something close to disappearing.

explain_en: General; something ceases to exist, like a language or right. 소멸되다 is for something that existed and has completely gone. In daily talk 사라지다 is more common, and 소멸되다 fits big things such as a language, a village or a right slowly disappearing. Points or coupons that expire are also said to be 소멸되다.

t90.ax: Old dialects are gradually dying out.
